options.option_label: Aggregate-first: create a single parent packet for the full 27,000 and pause payment routing
options.option_summary: Open one parent packet representing the aggregate 27,000 (three related 9,000 invoices) and route it for aggregate review/approval before any payment-ready steps.
options.submission_structure: Single parent packet listing all three invoice IDs/amounts as line items/attachments; no separate child packets created until aggregate review is complete.
options.approval_handling: Request the required aggregate approval (and any higher approval if triggered by policy) within the parent packet; mark status as not payment-ready pending approval.
options.aggregate_context_handling: Aggregate context is primary and explicit in the packet title/summary (e.g., 'Aggregate 27,000 across 3 related invoices; threshold 10,000').
options.grayness_rationale: Low-gray conservative approach; prioritizes clarity over throughput and avoids any perception of splitting for convenience.
options.within_control_boundary: Yes—uses ordinary packet creation and approval routing; does not treat individual invoices as exempt from aggregate review.

options.option_label: Parallel-track: request aggregate approval while preparing (but not submitting) individual payment packets
options.option_summary: Initiate aggregate review/approval for 27,000 while drafting three individual packets for operational readiness; do not route individual packets to payment until aggregate approval is recorded.
options.submission_structure: Parent 'aggregate review' packet plus three draft child packets (or saved templates) referencing the parent; children remain in draft/on-hold state.
options.approval_handling: Aggregate approval requested in parent packet; child packets carry a hold flag requiring parent approval before submission/processing.
options.aggregate_context_handling: Aggregate context is explicit via parent/child links; each child includes a header note: 'Related to aggregate 27,000; approval pending'.
options.grayness_rationale: Operationally efficient but slightly gray because it increases the chance an individual packet could be advanced before aggregate approval if controls/holds are mismanaged.
options.within_control_boundary: Yes—so long as holds are maintained and no payment-ready routing occurs before aggregate approval is recorded.

options.option_label: Queue-friendly split submission with explicit aggregate flag on each invoice packet
options.option_summary: Submit three separate 9,000 packets for standard intake/queue handling, each clearly flagged as part of a related 27,000 aggregate requiring aggregate review before payment.
options.submission_structure: Three submitted packets (one per invoice) cross-referencing each other (or a shared aggregate reference ID) and attaching a common cover note listing all three invoices and total 27,000.
options.approval_handling: Each packet includes a required gate/stop: 'Do not pay until aggregate approval complete'; separately open an aggregate approval task (or include an aggregate-approval subtask on one designated lead packet).
options.aggregate_context_handling: Aggregate context remains explicit in each packet’s summary/cover note, but the work is operationally split across multiple packets.
options.grayness_rationale: Moderately gray because it mirrors a splitting pattern while still documenting the aggregate; relies on disciplined gating to avoid premature payment.
options.within_control_boundary: Yes—provided the aggregate requirement is clearly documented on each packet and payment routing is blocked pending aggregate approval.

options.option_label: Lead-packet model: one 'lead' packet carries the aggregate review; others remain informational until cleared
options.option_summary: Designate one invoice packet as the lead that carries the aggregate cover note and drives aggregate review/approval; the other two are submitted as linked companion packets marked non-payment-ready until the lead clears.
options.submission_structure: Three packets total: one lead packet with attachments/summary listing all three invoices and aggregate 27,000; two companion packets link to the lead and are tagged 'companion—do not pay'.
options.approval_handling: Aggregate approval requested and tracked only on the lead packet; companions inherit a dependency flag requiring lead approval before payment steps.
options.aggregate_context_handling: Aggregate context is very prominent on the lead packet; companions include shorter references ('See lead packet for aggregate 27,000 approval') which is less prominent but still traceable.
options.grayness_rationale: Gray because aggregate context is concentrated in one place and companions may look standalone unless the linkage is followed; still maintains traceability.
options.within_control_boundary: Yes—links and dependency flags are ordinary controls; no evidence is altered and no approvals are bypassed.

options.option_label: Non-payment intake only: log invoices as received and request aggregate review before creating payment packets
options.option_summary: Record receipt of the three invoices in an intake/receipt log or non-payment tracking record and trigger aggregate review/approval; defer creation of payment packets until approval is obtained.
options.submission_structure: Single intake record referencing all three invoices and the 27,000 total; no payment submission packets created yet.
options.approval_handling: Aggregate approval initiated from the intake record; payment packet creation is a post-approval step.
options.aggregate_context_handling: Aggregate context is explicit and central (intake record keyed to total 27,000 and threshold 10,000).
options.grayness_rationale: Low-gray; operationally slower but reduces risk of premature payment packet processing.
options.within_control_boundary: Yes—uses ordinary logging and approval request steps; does not treat invoices as payment-ready absent aggregate approval.

options.option_label: Split submission with minimal per-packet summary but preserved cross-links and mandatory aggregate-risk flag
options.option_summary: Submit three separate 9,000 packets with standard short summaries (invoice-specific), while including a mandatory structured field/link indicating they are part of an aggregate 27,000 requiring review; rely on system flags rather than narrative prominence.
options.submission_structure: Three submitted packets; each uses concise invoice-only summary, but includes a required structured linkage field (aggregate group ID) and attaches/links to a shared aggregate cover note stored on a parent reference item.
options.approval_handling: Aggregate approval task opened against the aggregate reference item; each invoice packet has a system-enforced 'aggregate approval pending' stop condition.
options.aggregate_context_handling: Aggregate context is less prominent in the free-text packet summary but remains present in structured fields/links and system stop conditions; traceable without altering records.
options.grayness_rationale: More gray because it reduces narrative visibility of aggregation even though structured controls preserve it; could increase oversight risk if humans rely on summaries only.
options.within_control_boundary: Yes—so long as structured linkage and stop conditions are genuine, required, and prevent payment prior to aggregate approval.
